Self-metathesis of two molecules gives

\[
2\,\ce{CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH2CH3}
\longrightarrow
\ce{(CH3CH2)(CH3)CH-CH=CH-CH(CH3)(CH2CH3)}+\ce{CH2=CH2}
\]

Each half of the product retains one pre-existing stereogenic center, which may be \(R\) or \(S\). Thus the possible pairings are:

- \(R,R\)
- \(S,S\)
- \(R,S\) (equivalent to \(S,R\) by molecular symmetry)

The newly formed double bond can be \(E\) or \(Z\). Therefore,

\[
3 \times 2 = 6
\]

possible products are obtained, excluding ethene.

Answer: D
